stories.head: Iran's Revolutionary Guards declare Strait of Hormuz closed
stories.say: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the Strait of Hormuz is closed to ships of all nationalities, after claiming on Saturday that two tankers caught fire after hitting mines.
stories.stand: The IRGC Navy says passage through the strait is banned, as reports of tankers hit near the waterway mount.
body: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said on Saturday that the Strait of Hormuz was closed, according to the state news agency IRNA. It said ships of any nationality were barred from passing through.

The Guards said two oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the strait. IRNA said the vessels had switched off their tracking systems and tried an unauthorised route. There was no independent confirmation.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported at least two other tankers hit off Saudi Arabia's coast, Middle East Eye said. Iran's navy also reported a tanker on fire in the Sea of Oman.
Iran says it has stepped up attacks in response to the US blockade of its ports. On Wednesday, a container ship and a bulk carrier sank near the strait after being hit by projectiles.

stories.head: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats' convoy in West Bank
stories.say: Masked Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of French, Belgian and Polish diplomats near Taybeh in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, knocking a French mayor to the ground.
stories.stand: Israel's foreign minister condemned the attack during the olive harvest, and police have opened an investigation.
body: Masked settlers confronted a convoy of European diplomats and officials near the village of Taybeh on Saturday. The group had come to visit Palestinian olive harvesters.
Witnesses said stones were thrown and car windows smashed, including on a Belgian consulate vehicle. Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was assaulted and knocked down.

Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned what he called severe violence by Israeli rioters. The military said the tour had not been coordinated with its forces. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation.
Belgium's foreign minister, Maxime Prevot, said he would push for more EU sanctions, Al Jazeera reported. France's Jean-Noel Barrot urged Israel to arrest those responsible.

stories.head: Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine and cut power to a million
stories.say: Russian attacks across nine Ukrainian regions on Friday killed at least eight people and injured sixty, officials said, and left more than a million people briefly without power.
stories.stand: Drones hit shopping centres and energy sites as the UN warns early October was among the deadliest periods for civilians in years.
body: Russian attacks on Friday killed at least eight people and wounded 60, Ukrainian officials said. Nine regions were hit, including two shopping centres.
In Kharkiv, governor Oleh Syniehubov said two people died and 12 were wounded. Two were killed in Kramatorsk and two in Dnipropetrovsk region, with one death each in Volyn and Rivne.
Ukraine's energy ministry said power had been restored to more than a million people cut off by the strikes. Lutsk's mayor warned of a blackout of at least a day.
UN monitors said at least 328 civilians were killed in September. Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted 644 Ukrainian drones overnight, disrupting Moscow airports.

stories.head: Albanian police fire rubber bullets on fifth day of student protests
stories.say: Albanian police fired rubber bullets at protesters in Tirana on Saturday, the fifth day of student-led demonstrations demanding that Prime Minister Edi Rama resign.
stories.stand: Seven officers have been suspended as protests over corruption and education spread, while Rama refuses to step down.
body: Police used rubber bullets for the first time in the protests on Saturday, alongside tear gas and water cannon. Demonstrators threw stones and petrol bombs and set vehicles alight.
National police chief Skender Hita said all means had been used in a limited manner. Seven officers have been suspended over allegations that they exceeded their authority.
Students cite high fees, poor facilities, joblessness and alleged corruption. The wider movement began with opposition to a coastal resort project linked to Jared Kushner.
Rama has rejected calls to resign. He said on Saturday that the government respects students' right to protest, and has blamed opponents for encouraging violence.

stories.head: Three men jailed for 158 years over Mexico surfer killings
stories.say: A judge in Ensenada has jailed three men for one hundred and fifty-eight years each for killing Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad.
stories.stand: The three surfers were shot and their bodies left in a well during a trip to Baja California in April 2024.
body: A judge in Ensenada, Baja California, sentenced three men on Friday to 158 years and nine months each. They were named in court as Jesus Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus.
They were convicted a week earlier of homicide and violent robbery offences. The victims were killed on a surfing trip in April 2024, and their bodies were found in a well in May.
Prosecutors had sought 210 years each, Al Jazeera reported. The judge also ordered reparations to the families, according to ABC News.
The Robinson brothers' parents said no sentence would bring their sons back. The defence has indicated it will appeal.

stories.head: Sudan army says it hit RSF in Nyala; RSF says 30 killed at market
stories.say: Sudan's army says air strikes on Nyala on Friday killed dozens of RSF fighters. The RSF says a drone hit a livestock market there, killing thirty civilians.
stories.stand: The two sides give sharply different accounts of strikes on the South Darfur capital, the seat of the RSF's rival administration.
body: Sudan's army said on Friday that it destroyed RSF command centres in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Al Jazeera reported the army's claim that dozens of fighters were killed.
The RSF said a drone struck a busy livestock market in the city, killing 30 civilians, including 17 women and five children. A hospital source told AFP that 30 died and 47 were wounded.
The army has not commented on the market strike. The rights group Emergency Lawyers said the market was hit. The RSF has not addressed the army's claim about its fighters.
The war, which began in April 2023, has killed tens of thousands and displaced more than 11 million people.

stories.head: China jails kindergarten owner for life over lead poisoning of children
stories.say: A Chinese court has jailed a kindergarten operator for life after lead-tainted food poisoned more than two hundred children in Tianshui. The principal got fifteen years.
stories.stand: Staff added lead-containing paint to food to make it look appealing, the court found, in a case that shocked China in 2025.
body: The Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court sentenced kindergarten operator Li Huifang to life in prison on Friday. Executive principal Zhu Jinglin received 15 years and a 300,000 yuan fine.
Kitchen workers were jailed for six to eight years, according to state media. The defendants were convicted of producing and selling toxic and harmful food.
The court found that toxic, lead-containing pigments were added to food to make it look more appealing. Xinhua said 247 of 251 children tested had abnormal blood lead levels.
Xinhua said provincial disciplinary authorities had investigated 10 local officials over the case at the kindergarten in Tianshui, Gansu province.

stories.head: Hampshire police chief seeks £800,000 over small-boat landings
stories.say: Hampshire's police and crime commissioner says policing small-boat landings and protests has cost more than eight hundred thousand pounds, and she wants the Home Office to pay.
stories.stand: Donna Jones has written twice to the Home Secretary asking for full reimbursement and a halt to landings on the Hampshire coast.
body: Hampshire's police and crime commissioner, Donna Jones, says policing costs linked to small-boat landings in Portsmouth and Gosport have passed £800,000 since September.
She has written a second time to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. She wants the full cost repaid and future deployments funded. She says her first letter received no reply.
At the latest Gosport landing, police made 12 arrests, four of them for assaulting an officer. Jones also wants details of talks with France about the Normandy-to-Hampshire route.
The Home Office said there was no excuse for intimidating behaviour at some protests. It says it has contingency plans for arrivals elsewhere.

stories.head: Russell Brand trial hears from former flatmate
stories.say: Russell Brand's trial has heard a former flatmate describe him as very egotistical and preoccupied with sex. Brand denies all seven charges, including three of rape.
stories.stand: The comedian denies rape and sexual assault charges involving six women between 1999 and 2009 at Southwark Crown Court.
body: Russell Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court has continued, with a former flatmate giving evidence for the prosecution.
The witness told jurors Brand was very egotistical and erratic, and that sex was a major preoccupation for him on nights out.
The court also heard statements from two friends of the woman behind the 1999 rape allegation. Brand denies three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.
The defence is expected to argue that consensual encounters have been reimagined in recent years. The trial continues.

stories.head: Swinney pledges to bring Scotland's buses under public control
stories.say: John Swinney says Scotland's buses will be brought back under public control by twenty thirty-one, with the two pound fare cap reaching Aberdeen from April.
stories.stand: The First Minister told the SNP conference that franchising and regulation would give regional bodies more say over routes and fares.
body: John Swinney told the SNP conference in Aberdeen on Saturday that buses would return to public control by the end of this parliament.
The change would come through franchising and regulation rather than state ownership, giving regional transport partnerships more control over routes and fares. A Bill is due at Holyrood next year.
The £2 bus fare cap, now in greater Glasgow and the Highlands and Islands, will extend to Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire from April.
McGill's Buses, Scotland's largest independent operator, said it would resist the plans. Scottish Labour's Jackie Baillie welcomed the bus pledges.

stories.say: A sixteen-year-old boy and an eighty-year-old man have died after a light aircraft crashed near Drymen on Friday. Air accident investigators have sent a team to the site.
stories.stand: The aircraft had taken off from Glasgow Airport shortly before it came down north-east of the village on Friday afternoon.

The Air Accidents Investigation Branch has sent a team to gather evidence. Police have placed temporary airspace restrictions, including on drones, around the area.

stories.stand: The housing secretary would not say whether the housing benefit freeze will change at the 28 October Budget.
body: Housing Secretary Angela Rayner says she is confident the pledge to offer every rough sleeper a bed will be met. She accepts not everyone will take it.

Police said he had used his phone several times while driving, including to log on to a gambling website. He was banned from driving for 10 years and four months.

stories.head: Undercover film shows Reform figures calling for migrant camps
stories.say: Undercover ITV footage shows an aspiring Reform MP calling for camps for small-boat migrants. Reform says there is no room for racism and some people have been suspended.
stories.stand: The year-long investigation, airing on Sunday night, also records councillors talking about executing grooming gang members.
body: An ITV Exposure reporter spent a year undercover inside Reform UK. New footage released on Saturday shows aspiring MP Jason Powell calling for small-boat migrants to be held in camps.
Hounslow councillor Adam Parkins was recorded saying he would execute grooming gang members. Board member Gawain Towler said he had been racist every day at school, a view he now says appals him.
Reform says it has improved vetting, that not everyone filmed is a member, and that some people have been suspended. Three councillors have resigned and two have left the party.
Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said Nigel Farage shares responsibility. The documentary airs on ITV at 10.20pm on Sunday.

stories.head: Trump waives new Russia sanctions, drawing bipartisan criticism
stories.say: Donald Trump has waived new sanctions on Russia under the Graham Act just before they took effect. Republican and Democratic senators criticised the move.
stories.stand: The late-Friday order suspends tariffs and penalties on Russia and its oil buyers that Congress passed by large margins.
body: President Trump signed an order late on Friday waiving sanctions under the Graham Act. They had been due to take effect on Sunday.
The law would have imposed steep tariffs on buyers of Russian oil and gas. The White House said enforcing it now would hinder peace negotiations.
Republican senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn criticised the move, as did Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. Ukraine's President Zelensky also criticised the waiver.
Congress is in recess until after the 3 November midterms, so a quick response is unlikely.

stories.stand: With just over two weeks until the 3 November midterms, both camps used Saturday to try to drive turnout.
body: President Trump held a rally at Northern Kentucky University in Highland Heights on Saturday, backing Senate candidate Andy Barr and House candidate Ed Gallrein.

He repeated a pledge of $5,000 for every adult if Republicans win both chambers. He also tied a $100 million Kentucky drug plant investment to a Republican win. He called Rep. Thomas Massie a jerk and a loser.
No Kings rallies across the country urged people to vote early. The Justice Department on Friday warned officials handling ballots from suspected noncitizens that they could face prosecution.

stories.stand: The First Minister's first keynote since May's election also promised a misogyny offence and wider bus fare caps.
body: John Swinney closed the SNP conference in Aberdeen on Saturday with his first keynote since winning a mandate as First Minister in May.
He said he was determined to deliver independence and launched a campaign which he said had a six-figure war chest. No referendum timetable was given.
He announced a three-year £30 million fund for groups countering racism and a Bill to make misogyny-based harassment a specific offence. Members also backed a motion supporting a UK-wide ban on X.

stories.stand: Lord Ricketts also dismissed the Prime Minister's idea of Britain acting as a bridge between Washington and Kyiv.
body: Lord Ricketts, a former national security adviser, says ministers should be honest with the public about the threat from Russia. He also once ran the Foreign Office.

He rejected Andy Burnham's idea of the UK as a bridge between the US and Ukraine. He said Britain had little short-term sway over President Trump.

stories.head: IMF chief sees 'optimism and worry' as Bangkok meetings end
stories.say: Closing the IMF meetings in Bangkok on Saturday, Kristalina Georgieva said poorer countries now spend fourteen per cent of revenue on debt payments, up from eight.
stories.stand: Kristalina Georgieva said poorer, oil-importing countries face the hardest squeeze from war-driven energy prices and rising debt costs.
body: The IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok ended on Saturday. IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva said talks had been marked by both optimism and worry about the global outlook.
She cited the economy's resilience, the promise of AI and Asia's growth as reasons for optimism. Her worries included AI, inflation, high debt, wars and climate risks.

Georgieva said debt repayments by low-income countries had risen from 8% to 14% of government revenue in recent years. The IMF says low-income oil importers are most exposed to energy prices that have risen since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February.

She also warned that relying on AI investment as the single driver of growth leaves economies vulnerable. Saudi finance minister Mohammed al-Jadaan, who chairs the IMF's steering committee, warned that conflicts could disrupt key trade routes.

stories.head: Fed chair Warsh gives no hint on next rate move
stories.say: Speaking in Bangkok on Friday, Kevin Warsh said the Fed does not prejudge meetings, giving no signal on rates. US inflation rose to three point seven per cent in September.
stories.stand: Speaking in Bangkok before the Fed's 28 October decision, Kevin Warsh praised the economy's resilience but warned the AI transition would be bumpy.

They found a hearth and a pit that the team says may mark the earliest habitation structure in North America. The site's name means "They Were There" in an Athabascan language.

Finance is expected to dominate. The framework calls for $200bn a year for nature. A Global Landscapes Forum analysis says the Cali Fund for genetic data has received only $6,000.

stories.say: Qualcomm has rejected a Korean report that its newest flagship chip overheated in Samsung's Galaxy S27 Ultra tests. Its marketing chief said there are no systemic thermal issues.
stories.stand: The report suggested Samsung could switch to its own Exynos chips for next year's Galaxy S27 Ultra; Samsung has not commented.
body: Qualcomm has denied a South Korean report that its Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip overheated in Samsung's internal Galaxy S27 Ultra tests.
Chief marketing officer Don McGuire wrote on X that there are no systemic thermal issues. He said phone makers tune chips to balance performance and power.
The report said Samsung could use its own Exynos 2700 chip instead. Reviewers noted that McGuire's post named the standard 8 Elite Gen 6, not the Extreme variant at issue.
No Samsung statement has been reported.

stories.head: Street Fighter heads for top spot at North American box office
stories.say: Street Fighter is on course to top the North American box office, with an estimated thirty-one million dollars on its opening weekend after taking thirteen million on Friday.
stories.stand: The video game adaptation leads the weekend, while an A24 documentary about Elizabeth Holmes runs well ahead of expectations.
body: Street Fighter took about $13m on Friday from 3,575 cinemas in North America and is projected to open with about $31m. Weekend figures are estimates.
The film is directed by Kitao Sakurai and stars Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji.
In second place, You Can See Everything, a documentary about Elizabeth Holmes by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is tracking towards about $12m to $13m from 855 cinemas.
Disney's Whalefall is estimated at about $7m to $7.5m, while last weekend's leader, Other Mommy, fell to around $7.85m.

stories.head: Irish bookshops report surge in Sally Rooney sales after UK supply halt
stories.say: Irish bookshops report soaring sales of Sally Rooney novels, with one Galway shop selling ten times its usual number, after her publisher stopped supplying them in the UK.
stories.stand: Booksellers say orders from Britain are rising after Faber stopped supplying the author's books in the UK over her support for Palestine Action.
body: Booksellers in Ireland and Northern Ireland say demand for Sally Rooney's books has jumped since Faber said on Wednesday it would stop supplying them in the UK.
Kennys Bookshop in Galway told The Irish Times its Rooney sales had risen tenfold, with more orders from the UK. A bookshop in Co Down said sales had more than quadrupled.
A Belfast shop sold out by Friday morning and restocked from a Dublin wholesaler, the paper reported.

The Booksellers Association says UK shops may sell existing stock but can no longer order the titles. Faber says UK anti-terrorism law stops it passing on her earnings, as she supports the banned group Palestine Action.

stories.head: De Kooning sets European record at Sotheby's London sale
stories.say: Sotheby's London contemporary evening sale raised forty-five point nine million pounds on Thursday, led by a Willem de Kooning that set the artist's European auction record.
stories.stand: The Frieze week auction fell slightly short of last year's total, with records for de Kooning, a Hockney iPad drawing and Michael Andrews.
body: Sotheby's contemporary evening sale in London on 15 October raised £45.9m including fees, against £47.6m at the equivalent sale last year.
The hammer total of £36.9m fell below the presale low estimate. Of 34 lots offered after three were withdrawn, 28 sold.
Willem de Kooning's Untitled (1977) made £9.8m with fees, a European auction record for the artist. Gerhard Richter's Abstraktes Bild (1992) fetched £6.7m.
A David Hockney iPad drawing set a record for his works in that medium, and Michael Andrews's Butterfly Fish sold for £704,000, a record for his works on paper.

stories.head: Jodar and Davidovich Fokina set up all-Spanish Shanghai Masters final
stories.say: Rafael Jodar, aged twenty, beat Daniil Medvedev in straight sets on Saturday, and will face Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who came from a set down to beat Alexander Zverev.
stories.stand: Two Spaniards seeking a first Masters 1000 title will meet in Sunday's Shanghai final after beating Medvedev and top seed Zverev.
body: Rafael Jodar, 20, beat Daniil Medvedev 6-3, 6-4 in Saturday's first semi-final in Shanghai. It was his first straight-sets win of the week and his first Masters 1000 final.
Medvedev, the 2019 Shanghai champion, saved four set points in the first set but could not hold on. Jodar began the season ranked 168th.
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, 27, beat top seed Alexander Zverev 5-7, 6-4, 6-3. He has now won nine straight matches in China, including a title in Chengdu.
Zverev said fatigue and ankle discomfort affected him, Dawn reported. He is set to finish the year as world number one regardless.

stories.head: Man City beat Ipswich as Maresca sets Premier League record
stories.say: Erling Haaland scored twice as Manchester City beat Ipswich three-two on Saturday, making Enzo Maresca the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.
stories.stand: City stayed top with a seventh straight league win, while Liverpool beat nine-man Brentford and Chelsea won at Everton.
body: Manchester City beat Ipswich Town 3-2 at the Etihad on Saturday. Phil Foden scored first and Erling Haaland added two, taking him to 12 league goals this season.

Daizen Maeda equalised for Ipswich soon after Foden's opener, and Zian Flemming scored a late penalty. City say Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge.
Liverpool came from behind to win 2-1 at Brentford, with Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak scoring. Brentford had Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt sent off and lost for the first time this season.
Chelsea won 2-0 at Everton, with Pedro Neto scoring both goals, according to ANI.

stories.head: Tonga beat England 30-12 in Rugby League World Cup
stories.say: Tonga beat England thirty points to twelve in Perth on Saturday, with Haumole Olakau'atu scoring twice, leaving England's hopes of reaching the semi-finals in doubt.
stories.stand: Four tries to two in Perth put Tonga in a strong position in their pool and left England needing help from other results.
body: Tonga beat England 30-12 in their Rugby League World Cup opener at HBF Park in Perth on Saturday. The sell-out crowd of 18,302 included Tonga's King Tupou VI.
Stefano Utoikamanu scored the first try and two Isaiya Katoa penalties gave Tonga a 10-0 half-time lead. Haumole Olakau'atu scored twice and Tolutau Koula once.
AJ Brimson and Dom Young scored England's tries. Katoa was named player of the match.
Tonga hold the head-to-head advantage over England in the pool. England still face France and Papua New Guinea, while Tonga play Samoa on 1 November.

stories.head: Rain washes out India v West Indies decider as T20 series ends 2-2
stories.say: Rain ended the fifth Twenty20 between India and West Indies in Bengaluru on Saturday, with India on one hundred and eighteen for five, so the series finished two-all.
stories.stand: The deciding match in Bengaluru was cut to nine overs a side and then abandoned, denying West Indies a first series win in India since 2002.
body: The fifth and final Twenty20 international between India and West Indies was abandoned because of rain in Bengaluru on Saturday.
After a long rain delay, the match was cut to nine overs a side. West Indies won the toss and India reached 118 for five in 7.4 overs before rain returned.
Ishan Kishan made 30 from 10 balls and Naman Dhir 24 not out from six. The series ended 2-2, and the trophy was shared.
